Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-14 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~62 minutes | Location: Zoom | Host: Liam Park
Attendees: Liam Park, Maya Reddy, Sophie Martinez, Ethan Cole, Priya Nair, Noah Kim, Isabella Rossi + company-wide All-Hands

Summary (auto): Leadership overview of Q3 results, product roadmap updates (Dedicated & Private), hiring and org changes, compliance progress, customer wins, and Q4 priorities.

[00:00:00] Liam Park: All right, good afternoon everyone, welcome to the October all-hands, um, thanks for joining. Quick housekeeping, we'll run through a few slides, then Q&A. If you have questions put them in chat, we'll come back to them.

[00:00:22] Liam Park: First up — Q3 recap. Overall I'm really proud, revenue growth was ahead of plan, churn stayed low, and we've got some strong momentum on Dedicated contracts. There were some pockets where latency SLOs slipped during bursts, Ethan you wanna speak to that?

[00:00:39] Ethan Cole: Yeah thanks Liam, um so the burst events — we saw two incidents where autoscaling didn't return capacity quick enough because of, uh, a cold-start issue in our Dedicated pool. Root cause was a kernel scheduling conflict on one host class, we rolled mitigation to route to fallback variants, and now the fix is tested — we have a hot-pool config and a better warm-start path. Not perfect but we're improving.

[00:01:12] Speaker 5: sorry can you repeat the warm-start path bit?

[00:01:16] Ethan Cole: Yeah, so warm-start path means pre-initialized processes with KV cache primed for common model prefixes, so request latency doesn't include full model load. We found some edge cases with model quantization profiles where priming failed. Fix is in PR, will deploy to canary next week.

[00:01:38] Liam Park: Good, thanks. On the business side — Sophie, product and roadmap?

[00:01:44] Sophie Martinez: Hi all — quick roadmap highlights. We're prioritizing Dedicated capacity improvements, faster model variant routing, and expanding the Private onboarding flow (VPC-first, and an on-prem install guide). Also shipping Redwood Optimize 2.0 which includes smarter batching suggestions and a UI for quantization recommendations.

[00:02:07] Sophie Martinez: We're also going to pilot a self-service Dedicated quickstart for mid-market customers, with three predefined profiles: latency-optimized, cost-optimized, balanced. We'll have a beta by mid-November.

[00:02:22] Speaker 3: How will the quickstart handle security controls for SOC2 customers?

[00:02:27] Maya Reddy: Good question. The quickstart will still require enterprise onboarding for KMS/HSM integrations and RBAC toggles. The idea is to automate the routine network and capacity provisioning while gating sensitive integrations behind a short manual step. We expect that to shorten time-to-pilot from weeks to days for many customers.

[00:02:44] Liam Park: Speaking of SOC2 — Maya, update on compliance timeline?

[00:02:48] Maya Reddy: We're on track for SOC2 Type II in Q1 2026, auditor engaged, evidence collection started. We still need to close a few items: formal change management docs, some logging retention configs, and a minor remediation in key rotation automation. Security will publish an internal doc with owners and dates later this week.

[00:03:06] Priya Nair: On the GTM side — pipeline looks healthy, we closed two mid-market Dedicated deals this quarter, and we have a couple of enterprise POCs that could convert in Q4. We're seeing a common ask: private deployments with strict data residency plus predictable latency. That's driving a lot of inbound.

[00:03:24] Priya Nair: We're also seeing competitive pressure from BigCloud AI on price, and EdgeServe on on-prem capabilities, so we need tight messaging on our reliability and cost controls.

[00:03:36] Liam Park: Great. Noah — customer success highlight?

[00:03:39] Noah Kim: Customer wins — spotlight on SynthHealth, they moved from a POC to Dedicated, reduced generation cost by ~28% with our batching and cache config, and their latency 95th percentile met their SLA after we tuned KV cache profiles. We'll post a short case study with metrics. Also a small number of customers flagged audit log gaps, working to add more granular event logging.

[00:04:05] Speaker 2: Any update on international regions or APAC rollout?

[00:04:09] Liam Park: We're expanding dedicated capacity in EU and planning a pilot in APAC next quarter with a partner. More details in the roadmap doc Sophie will share.

[00:04:21] Isabella Rossi: Quick HR note — hiring: we're hiring 30 engineers across runtime, infra, and platform through Q4, plus product and sales hires. Referral bonus reminder — see the internal hiring link. Also we'll be updating parental leave policy next month, details to follow.

[00:04:41] Speaker 7: Org changes?

[00:04:43] Liam Park: Small changes — we moved the infra reliability team under Engineering to streamline incident response, and created a new Applied ML team under Research to focus on inference optimizations and evals. Maya will lead Applied ML.

[00:04:57] Maya Reddy: Yes, excited about Applied ML — goal is to close the loop between performance experiments and production rollout faster. We'll run monthly eval cycles tied to quality regression alerts.

[00:05:11] Liam Park: Okay let's open to questions from the chat — I see a few.

[00:05:18] Chat question: Are there plans for an on-prem appliance?

[00:05:22] Sophie Martinez: Short answer: yes, on-prem appliance is on the roadmap but not GA; we'll offer an opinionated package for large regulated customers. The first cut will be a validated installer and config set; full air-gapped/installer support targeted in H2 2026.

[00:05:40] Chat question: Any change to pricing?

[00:05:42] Priya Nair: No immediate pricing changes. We are piloting model-based quantization credits for high-volume users to encourage cost-saving configs, but list pricing remains stable.

[00:05:55] Speaker 4: On the technical side, are we prioritizing GPU selection or kernel selection for latency wins?

[00:06:01] Ethan Cole: Both — kernel selection gives us quick wins across hardware, but underlying GPU topology influences batching and kernel effectiveness. We're investing in smarter kernel selection heuristics and a hardware capability registry to route requests optimally.

[00:06:17] Liam Park: Note on metrics — we'll publish a postmortem on the autoscaling incidents and a follow-up doc with the warm-pool config. Expect that by Monday.

[00:06:28] Speaker 6: Any legal/procurement changes?

[00:06:31] Liam Park: We're streamlining the standard SOW and MSA templates to reduce legal cycle time; procurement will have a new self-serve guide for mid-market later this quarter.

[00:06:42] Liam Park: Alright, quick lightning round — what's one thing each leader asks the company to focus on for Q4?

[00:06:48] Ethan Cole: Improve canary fidelity and reduce warm-start failures.

[00:06:52] Maya Reddy: Close SOC2 evidence gaps and automate logging retention.

[00:06:56] Sophie Martinez: Ship the Dedicated quickstart beta and make onboarding smoother.

[00:07:00] Priya Nair: Convert two enterprise POCs and refine competitive pricing messages.

[00:07:04] Noah Kim: Publish customer case studies and fix audit log gaps.

[00:07:10] Liam Park: Okay thanks everyone. A couple of admin notes — town hall recording will be posted, and please complete the engagement survey by Friday.

[00:07:20] Liam Park: We'll wrap and move to a short AMA — pick your mic, ask questions.

[00:07:30] [ambient chatting, mics unmuted briefly]

[00:07:40] Speaker 8: Quick question about Dedicated pricing — will quickstart customers get a discount?

[00:07:44] Priya Nair: We'll offer a limited-time promo for beta customers, more details in the product notes.

[00:07:52] Speaker 9: Regarding SOC2, will the auditor reviews impact customer-facing docs?

[00:07:56] Maya Reddy: We'll update the security page and FAQ after Type II is complete, but any interim customer requests will be handled by our security team with temporary attestations where appropriate.

[00:08:10] Speaker 10: Are we tracking unit economics per model family?

[00:08:13] Sophie Martinez: Yes, Redwood Optimize 2.0 will surface per-model unit cost estimates, and we'll align it to billing metrics.

[00:08:20] Liam Park: Great. Last item — shoutouts. Big congrats to the infra team for the warm-pool patch, and to Sales for the SynthHealth close.

[00:08:32] [applause emoji in chat]

[00:08:36] Liam Park: Closing remarks — we're in a strong position, focus on reliability and customer onboarding will make the difference this quarter. Thanks everyone, meeting adjourned.

[00:08:50] End of recording.
